counterfactual_missing_items: No raw support for constrictive bronchiolitis (e.g., air trapping, mosaic attenuation) to indicate bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome
No raw support for drug-induced pneumonitis (e.g., eosinophilia, hypersensitivity reaction) linked to mycophenolate or tacrolimus
No evidence of active Pneumocystis infection at the time of new infiltrates, as repeat BAL was negative
decisive_items: alveoli filled with inflammatory debris consisting of granulation tissue, interstitial inflammation, and areas of intra-alveolar fibrin deposition
new patchy peribronchovascular consolidations in the right upper lobe, left upper lobe, and left lower-lobe apical segment
Repeat BAL was negative for AFB, fungus, and Pneumocystis jirovecii
response.rationale: The biopsy shows classic organizing pneumonia (granulation tissue, interstitial inflammation, intra-alveolar fibrin) and the new infiltrates appear after PCP treatment, fitting a post-infectious organizing pneumonia. R2 mislabels the same biopsy as bronchiolitis obliterans syndrome, which requires constrictive bronchiolitis, not intra-alveolar granulation tissue. R5 is based on the initial PCP that resolved, and R3/R6/R4 lack specific raw support for the current pulmonary process.

rejected.why: Initial BAL positivity for PCP was treated and resolved; repeat BAL was negative, and the new infiltrates and biopsy are not consistent with active PCP.
IgA nephropathy is the cause of ESRD but has no direct link to the current pulmonary findings.
Mycophenolate exposure is mentioned, but no raw support links it to the biopsy-proven organizing pneumonia pattern.
No raw support spans provided; tacrolimus-induced pneumonitis is speculative and not supported by the biopsy findings.
